# A two-limb number minus a limb, finite core

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `sub_2_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x - a$:

$$z \approx x - a.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finite::sub(x, a)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | the finite core: no fix-up of infinities and NaN |
| `finite::sub(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | the limb of the `Expansion<T, 1>` operand is the limb $a$ |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (x - a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x - a\rvert$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $2^{-105} \approx 2.4652 \times 10^{-32}$ | $2^{-47} \approx 7.1054 \times 10^{-15}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1p-47f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.0000000000001p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.000002p-47f`, `0.0f` |

The compiled constants are the entry `sub_limb` of `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 2>>`: `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the exact result, `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` relative to the computed one ($\lvert \text{error}\rvert \le \mathtt{unit\_computed}\,\lvert\text{computed}\rvert + \mathtt{tiny\_computed}$); `sub_limb` holds the larger constants of [`sub_2_1`](sub_2_1.md) and [`sub_1_2`](sub_1_2.md).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `sub_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Sign.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Sign.v), against `sub_2_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions sub_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition sub_2_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let '(z0, z1) := sub_2_1 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 a in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) - a)) <= 2 * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) - a).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `sub_2_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_2_1 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 4) on -a. **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/sub_2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/sub_2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md).

```
# x - a: a 2-limb number minus a number of the format, through add_2_1, whose claims it inherits.

n        = neg(a)
(z0, z1) = add_2_1(x0, x1, n)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#sub_2_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 058 772 | 0 | 0.540731 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 056 882 | 0 | 0.665474 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 12 218 888 | 0 | 0.939450 (`fp:5:-4:2`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`sub_2_1_full`](sub_2_1_full.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
